sources.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved Players Can Jump Into Firefight for Free This Winter
sources.text: For nearly two decades, Firefight has been a Halo favorite, challenging Spartans to team up, hold the line, and survive wave after wave of enemies. The tradition continues this winter as we add the four-player cooperative PvE mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free update. We’re kicking things off tonight at XBOX FanFest, where attendees will be the first to jump in and experience Firefight across new maps and armed with plenty of weapons to help even the odds. And there’s more on the way. We’ll be sharing additional details about this free update at Halo Fest , happening December 12-13 in Seattle, WA, where fans attending the event will also have a chance to play Firefight throughout the weekend. We can’t wait to see you all at Halo Fest and to celebrate 25 years of Halo and XBOX together!

sources.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved – modo cooperativo Firefight chega em breve
sources.text: Há quase duas décadas, Firefight é um dos modos favoritos dos fãs de Halo, desafiando os Spartans a unir forças, defender suas posições e sobreviver a ondas e mais ondas de inimigos. A tradição continua em breve, quando adicionaremos o modo cooperativo PvE para quatro jogadores a Halo: Campaign Evolved em uma atualização gratuita. E vem mais por aí. Compartilharemos mais detalhes sobre essa atualização gratuita no Halo Fest , que acontece nos dias 12 e 13 de dezembro em Seattle, nos EUA. Os fãs presentes no evento também poderão jogar Firefight durante todo o fim de semana. Mal podemos esperar para encontrar vocês no Halo Fest e celebrar juntos os 25 anos de Halo e XBOX!

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved to Get Firefight as a Free Update
sources.text: When Halo: Campaign Evolved first came out in July it did not include any multiplayer modes, but the first-person shooter remake will at least get Firefight as a free update this winter. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the returning mode in a social media post Thursday, along with a graphic showing a team of Spartans shooting a mix of Covenant and Flood enemies with various guns. While Firefight isn't the arena competitive multiplayer that most fans had hoped from the Halo remake at launch, wave-based PvE has been a mainstay in the series since Halo 3: ODST in 2009. Essentially, you and your friends load into a map and fight increasingly difficult waves of enemies until you get overwhelmed. There's no reason to believe that this iteration is going to be any different. Regardless of whether or not Team Deathmatch comes to Halo: Campaign Evolved, this will be the first multiplayer mode to hit the remake, which was pitched primarily as a straight-up revival of the iconic Combat Evolved campaign. Multiplayer was the major piece missing from Campaign Evolved, and this could be a sign that more multiplayer modes will be added in the future. IGN's Halo: Combat Evolved remake gave it a 7 . We said: "Halo: Campaign Evolved speaks to the series' timelessness and adds a decent set of new missions, but it's a mostly a lean retread that's more of a test run for its future with Unreal Engine." This Firefight announcement comes as Xbox celebrates its 25th anniversary. Earlier today, Sharma looked ahead, predicting "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations." As for Halo, following the summer's drastic cuts at Microsoft's gaming business, Xbox announced a significant reshuffle that saw the next mainline Halo game handed to Call of Duty developer Activision , which is spinning up a new team to work on the franchise. Mass layoffs hit Halo Studios at the same time. Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved ‘Firefight’ update announced
sources.text: Publisher Xbox Game Studios and developer Halo Studios have announced a free update for Halo: Campaign Evolved , which will add the four-player cooperative player-versus-environment “Firefight” mode to the game. “For nearly two decades, Firefight has been a Halo favorite, challenging Spartans to team up, hold the line, and survive wave after wave of enemies. The tradition continues this winter as we add the four-player cooperative [player-versus-environment] mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free update.,” Halo Studios director of competitive engagement Tahir Hasangjekaj said. Hasangjekaj continued, “We’re kicking things off tonight at Xbox FanFest [in Seattle] , where attendees will be the first to jump in and experience Firefight across new maps and armed with plenty of weapons to help even the odds.” Further information will be announced at Halo Fest, which will run from December 12 to 13 in Seattle, Washington. Halo: Campaign Evolved is available now for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store . It is also available via Game Pass.

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved’s Next Big Update Will Add A Free Horde Mode
sources.text: Firefight Halo Halo: Campaign Evolved Xbox Halo: Campaign Evolved is getting a free update later this year that will add Firefight, the franchise’s popular wave-based horde mode, to the game. It’s likely to be the last bit of Halo content to be developed by what remains of Halo Studios as the series moves under Activision. Earlier this year, Xbox launched Halo: Campaign Evolved , which is set to be the last major Halo game developed by longtime franchise stewards Halo Studios, formerly 343 Industries. While the remake was fine, the $50 price tag felt high considering it didn’t include any multiplayer deathmatch mode or anything else beyond the campaign and some bonus missions you could play alone or with pals. So when it was reported in October that Firefight was going to be added to Campaign Evolved, fans were hopeful. And now Xbox has confirmed that Firefight is indeed being added to the remake soon. On November 12, Xbox announced via its official website that Firefight is being added to the remake as part of a free update planned to arrive this winter. Folks going to Halo Fest in December will get a chance to play it early before it’s added to the remake. Firefight in Campaign Evolved will support up to four players, just like the campaign’s co-op mode. Xbox didn’t share any other details about what to expect, but hopefully this is a classic Firefight experience like what we had in Halo: Rea ch and Halo 3: ODST , the game that introduced the wave-based horde mode to the series nearly 20 years ago. The previous report that claimed Firefight was in the works for the remake also reported that Theater Mode was set to be added as part of this free update. However, the report claimed the skeleton crew working on Campaign Evolved’ s last big update might not be able to pull all of its plans off before the studio is fully closed up for good. So for now, we don’t know if Theater Mode, letting players look at past gameplay clips via replays, will arrive this winter. But at the very least, a pretty good remake will be even better with the addition of Firefight. Considering it might be a while until we get a new Halo from Activision, now in charge of the series , this is likely the last bit of new Halo content fans will get for some time. sources.name: Video Games Chronicle
sources.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved is getting Firefight in a free update
sources.text: Firefight, a 4-player PvE mode, is coming to Halo: Campaign Evolved soon Xbox is adding Firefight mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free update this winter. Firefight has appeared in several Halo games and will come to Halo: Campaign Evolved as a 4-player PvE mode. There’s no release date just yet, but Xbox FanFest attendees will be able to play it later today. We’re told that more details about this Firefight update will come during Halo Fest, which is set to take place from December 12 – 13. Until then, all we know is that the update will be free and out sometime in the winter. Halo: Campaign Evolved was released in July of this year. It is a remake of the first Halo game’s story mode, and it was also the first game released under 343 Industries’ new name, Halo Studios . However, it will now likely be the only game released under the Halo Studios name, as the team was severely impacted by the recent layoffs across Xbox. As part of this, Xbox transferred Halo over to Activision , leaving a smaller Halo Studios in charge of Halo games that are already out, including Campaign Evolved. This upcoming winter update indicates that Xbox isn’t ready to abandon past Halo games just yet, but the future of the series is still uncertain. We know that a new Halo game is being developed by Activision, but we’ve received no indication as to whether this will continue where previous titles like Halo Infinite left off, or if we’ll see a soft reboot of the series under the new developers. Halo’s previous creative director Frank OâConnor recently shared his thoughts on the matter , urging Activision to hire talent from both Bungie and Halo Studios, since both have suffered layoffs. Right now, it’s unclear if any former devs were brought over to Activision when the studio was handed the Halo series.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sells in huge numbers, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge success for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, shifting more than 5.2 million copies in four days. Nintendo announced the sales result this morning in a press release, specifying that the record relates only to Nintendo-published games. But since Nintendo's games are the most popular Switch 2 games, the fastest-selling-ever title presumably holds. It's an incredible result for a game that's been received with enormous enthusiasm. Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time five golden stars in Eurogamer's review , saying: "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve." We've also already seen a jump in US Switch 2 sales because of the game's release. So much for not launching in November near GTA 6 , eh? This level of success begs the question of whether Nintendo would consider remaking more beloved old Zelda games - or Nintendo games - to replicate this nostalgia-driven effect. Are there other Zelda games that have the pull of Ocarina of Time that haven't been remade or remastered already in some capacity? If you're inspired to pick the game up because of this, or already have it, know that we've got a whole proverbial library shelf of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides to help you through the game.

sources.title: How to complete the Frog side quest in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: The Fabulous Five Froggish Tenors need five songs played to them in OoT, which unlocks a new minigame. The Frogs in The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time are found in the Zora River, and need songs played to them to complete their side quest. Referring to themselves as the Fabulous Five Froggish Tenors, Link's goal is to play five songs to them that they want to hear, which then unlocks a new minigame that you can play. If you can complete the frog song minigame, that then grants you a new piece of heart, a very valuable commodity. If you want to know how to complete this side quest, I'll take you through a full walkthrough below and what you need to know about the frogs and their love of music. To find the Five Froggish Tenors and start this side quest, you need to go to Zora River, which is accessed via the Northeast edge of Hyrule Field. Halfway along this route, on the North side, you'll find a small alcove with five pillars in it. This is where the Frogs are waiting. Simply interact with them like any NPC to begin the quest. You need to play several specific songs for the Frogs on your Ocarina for the chance to unlock the minigame, each one of which grants the players rupees as a reward. You need to play the following songs (in any order): As a bonus, players can also play the Song of Storms, learned from the Kakariko Windmill as an adult as part of a quest to learn the Lenses of Truth in Zelda Ocarina of Time . This isn't necessary to unlock the quest, but playing the Song of Storms for the frogs will grant you an additional piece of heart. Once all five necessary songs have been played, you can unlock the Frog Song minigame. Unfortunately, OoT doesn't actually explain how to control it, which can make it tricky. Here's how it works: Input it correctly, and you'll be awarded another piece of heart! sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is selling way more physical copies than digital in Japan
sources.text: Roughly two-thirds of its sales were physical The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is selling more physical copies and digital copies in Japan, and by some margin to boot. Japanese magazine Famitsu 's latest sales chart numbers are in, with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time unsurprisingly at the top. According to its data, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Nintendo Switch 2 sold 537,041 physical copies at Japanese retailers. Earlier this week, Nintendo confirmed that the latest Zelda release had sold over 5.2 million copies within four days of launch, making it "the highest global sales for any Nintendo-published Nintendo Switch 2 game in its first four days." Nintendo specified that 810,000 of these copies were sold in Japan. This means the Ocarina of Time remake sold around 272,959 digital copies in the region, roughly a third of the game's total sales in the region. With Sony 's decision to end physical disc production in 2028, and Rockstar releasing a ton of copies of GTA 6 today that feature nothing more than a code in a box that will activate in a week's time, there's been a lot of debate around physical game releases as of late. However, it's clear there's still a market out there for them, even if it is shrinking. Granted, Zelda's fortunes may have been helped by the fancy physical boxed copy that the game launched with, but even so, two-thirds of the game's sales in the region are certainly significant. stories.summary: The 44th Golden Joystick Awards took place last night, with Resident Evil Requiem winning four awards including Ultimate Game of the Year and Console Game of the Year. Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Resident Evil Requiem wins four Golden Joystick Awards, including Ultimate and Console GOTY
sources.text: Capcom receives seven awards, including Studio of the Year and recognition for Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword The 44th Golden Joystick Awards took place last night, with Resident Evil Requiem winning four awards including Ultimate Game of the Year and Console Game of the Year. The ninth instalment in the franchise also received Best Game Trailer, in addition to Angela Sant'Albano winning Best Lead Performer for her role as Grace Ashcroft. Capcom received seven awards, including Studio of the Year, Best Audio Design for Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and Best Supporting Performer for Grace Saif’s role as Diana in Pragmata. AdHoc's Dispatch earned Best Storytelling and Best Soundtrack. Meccha Chameleon was recognised as Best Indie Game (self-published), Best Multiplayer Game, Streamer’s Choice, and Developer’s Choice. Elsewhere, Remedy received Best Visual Design for Control Resonant, Unknown Worlds' Subnautica 2 won Best Early Access Game, Pearl Abyss's Crimson Desert was named PC Game of the Year, and House House's Big Walk received Critics' Choice. sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Crimson Desert wins 'PC Game of the Year' at the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards
sources.text: Resident Evil Requiem and Meccha Chameleon were the night's other big winners. There was some fun conversation here at PC Gamer recently about the anachronistic name of The Golden Joystick Awards, which are put on by PC Gamer's publisher. Who even uses a joystick anymore? Flight sim diehards, fighting game enthusiasts, and not many others. So why is it called that? Joysticks , really? Simply put, the name reflects the age of the awards, which debuted in 1983, making it the longest-running publicly-voted videogame awards show of all time, according to Wikipedia. Back in those days, joysticks were it, and trust me, they weren't the sweet pieces of hardware we have access to now. But we loved 'em! And we used them to play games like the Golden Joysticks' first-ever game of the year, Jetpac. It was a banger! Here we are, 43 years later, and much has changed: From a tiny ceremony handing out five trophies, the Golden Joysticks have grown to become one of the biggest videogame awards events of the year, watched by millions of people around the world on just about every streaming platform you can name. Yet that name, the Golden Joystick Awards , remains. Frankly, I'm glad about that. A little bit of reliability in this world is good for everyone. Which leads me to the point: The 44 th annual Golden Joystick Awards has now concluded, and the top gong , as my UK compatriots like to say for some reason—the Ultimate Game of the Year award, for the rest of us—has gone to Resident Evil Requiem , Capcom's latest tale of zombie-fueled bad news. Can't really argue with that call: PC Gamer's Elie Gould gave Resident Evil Requiem a whopping 92% score in their review , saying it "feels like you're playing a highlight reel of the best moments in the series." Requiem claimed three other wins on the night: Console Game of the Year, Best Game Trailer, and Best Lead Performer for Angela Sant'Albano's turn as Grace Ashcroft. Crimson Desert won for PC Game of the Year, which surprises me a bit given that it's also on consoles and pretty much the same experience. We liked that one too: Not quite as enthusiastically, but it still earned an enviable 80% review score . "Vast and obtuse in a way that is going to frustrate some and exhilarate others," as reviewer Mollie Taylor put it: "A fascinating journey, even when the destination isn't all that." Multiplayer hide-and-seek game Meccha Chameleon was the night's other big winner, taking home four awards for Best Multiplayer Game, Best Indie Game (self-published), the Steamers' Choice Award, and Developer's Choice Award. Dispatch won twice, for Best Storytelling and Best Soundtrack, and The Witcher also sort of claimed two wins as well: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered took the trophy for Best Remake/Remaster, while The Witcher 4 won for Most Wanted Game. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. So there you have it, 44 years down and hopefully many more to come—all of them bearing that glorious golden name. Here's your full list of 2026 Golden Joystick Awards winners: 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill. sources.title: Resident Evil Requiem actor after Golden Joystick Awards win: "Capcom, you cannot fail!"
sources.text: Resident Evil Requiem walked away with the biggest prize of the night at the Golden Joystick Awards yesterday, capping off a total of four wins with the prestigious title of Ultimate Game of the Year. But in an acceptance speech delivered on-stage by Leon Kennedy actor Nick Apostoledes, there was an allusion to an even bigger winner - Capcom itself. "What can I say?" Apostoledes began. "Resident Evil going 30 years strong this year - how fitting is it to win Ultimate Game of the Year for Requiem? We are just honored to be part of a project that is so beloved, a franchise that is so beloved. Thank you to the fans, thank you for keeping this alive. Capcom, you cannot fail." Apostoledes' remarks were followed up by pre-recorded comments from Requiem director Koshi Nakanishi, who said he was "thrilled" to accept the award, and spoke about how encouraging it was for a single-player game to win, especially in such a crowded field. While Resi itself will be making the big headlines, however, Apostoledes touched on an interesting point: the legendary run that Capcom itself is on. As well as claiming two GOTY titles for Requiem, that title also secured wins in the Best Game Trailer category, and a Best Lead Performer win for Grace Ashcroft actress Angela Sant'Albano. But two of Capcom's other titles - Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword - were also in contention for several categories, each one claiming its own win. Onimusha took the prize for Best Audio Design, while Diana actress Grace Saif took home Best Supporting Performer for her role in Pragmata. With three out of its four major releases this year claiming wins, perhaps it was of little surprise that Capcom would also take home the prize for Studio of the Year. 2026 has been a jewel in a crown that Capcom has been polishing for some time now. In the last four years, it's been on an excellent run. The last time a new release has slipped below a MetaCritic score of 80 was 2023's Exoprimal, and the closest thing it's had to a flop was Monster Hunter Wilds, which was plagued by performance issues. Elsewhere, it's been turning Resident Evil back into an essential release, breathing new life into classics, and successfully bringing life to new IP. It's been a relatively slow, quiet process, but Capcom has rarely put a foot wrong since 2020, and the community is starting to take note. 2027 looks like a quieter year for the studio, but with Resident Evil Veronica on the horizon, it looks like fans will still be eating pretty well. sources.title: Efeito GTA 6? Logitech cria dia de folga para funcionários jogarem videogame
sources.text: Lançamentos de games em NOVEMBRO de 2026 - Calendário VOXL Além do aguardado GTA 6, novembro traz remake de Ocarina of Time e mais de 30 jogos. Confira as estreias do mês. Crédito: Voxl A fabricante de acessórios para eletrônicos Logitech oficializou, nesta quarta-feira (10), um novo benefício curioso. A partir de agora, funcionários da companhia podem tirar um dia de folga remunerada apenas para se dedicar a videogames . A campanha se chama Gaming Time Off, ou GTO , e foi confirmada em um comunicado oficial pela própria CEO da companhia, Hanneke Faber. De forma bem humorada, ela mesma reconhece que o timing da revelação tem a ver com o lançamento de Grand Theft Auto 6 e com o provável número grande de ausências de pessoas no próprio emprego durante o primeiro dia de disponibilidade do game. “Para os funcionários da Logi que planejam uma viagem a Vice City, não é mais preciso pegar a “gripe GTA” — basta tirar o seu GTO”, brinca a executiva no LinkedIn . O GTO estará disponível para todos os funcionários da Logitech , mas o texto oficial não explica se há limitações sobre quando a folga pode ser tirada ou quantas pessoas da equipe conseguem sair no mesmo dia, por exemplo. De acordo com a fabricante, famosa por produtos como mouses, teclados e fones de ouvido, a folga é uma forma de reconhecer os “ benefícios cognitivos e profissionais ” da prática de jogos digitais. “É hora de deixar de lado o estereótipo de que jogar videogame é perda de tempo. Como uma empresa que desenvolve produtos tanto para o trabalho quanto para o lazer, observamos diariamente como o engajamento em uma dessas esferas favorece o desempenho na outra ”, complementa a CEO. O jogo da Rockstar sai em 19 de novembro deste ano e deve ser um dos maiores fenômenos recentes da indústria. O título já bateu recordes de pré-venda nos consoles e pode ser baixado antecipadamente por quem já fez a compra. sources.title: Logitech dará dia de folga para funcionários jogarem videogame; Brasil está incluído
sources.text: A Logitech anunciou uma iniciativa que promete agradar aos funcionários que gostam de videogames: um dia de folga dedicado exclusivamente aos jogos . Batizado de Logi Game Day , o benefício será oferecido aos colaboradores da empresa, incluindo os profissionais que trabalham no Brasil. A iniciativa marca o primeiro dia dedicado aos games em toda a história da Logitech e tem como objetivo reconhecer o papel dos videogames no desenvolvimento de habilidades que também podem ser utilizadas no ambiente profissional. O evento acontecerá em 19 de novembro de 2026 , mesma data prevista para o lançamento de GTA 6 . Segundo a empresa, a decisão está relacionada a pesquisas sobre a influência dos games no desenvolvimento de competências profissionais. Um levantamento da Logitech, chamado Ctrl Tomorrow , apontou que 81% dos jogadores entrevistados acreditam que os videogames contribuem para a autoconfiança, ajudam a reduzir a ansiedade e estão associados a um melhor desempenho nas atividades cotidianas. Outro estudo citado pela fabricante revelou que 98,8% dos profissionais responsáveis por decisões de tecnologia da informação consultados acreditam que habilidades desenvolvidas nos jogos podem ser aplicadas ao trabalho. Entre essas competências estão pensamento estratégico, resolução de problemas complexos e capacidade de atuar sob pressão. Os resultados representam percepções dos participantes das pesquisas e não comprovam, isoladamente, que jogar videogame melhora o desempenho profissional. “Chegou a hora de deixar para trás o estereótipo de que jogar é perda de tempo”, afirmou Hanneke Faber, CEO da Logitech. Para celebrar a iniciativa, a Logitech G realizará uma transmissão ao vivo diretamente de sua sede em San Jose, nos Estados Unidos, no dia 19 de novembro. O evento será apresentado por Robin Piispanen, gerente-geral da Logitech G e ex-jogador profissional. Segundo Piispanen, experiências em jogos como GTA 6 , Call of Duty e Forza podem estimular a colaboração e a resolução de problemas. A diretora de Recursos Humanos da Logitech, Elaine Laird, também destacou que reservar um período para atividades de lazer pode ajudar os colaboradores a retornar ao trabalho com novas perspectivas. Com o Logi Game Day, a fabricante passa a incorporar os videogames à sua política de benefícios, defendendo que jogar pode representar não apenas entretenimento, mas também uma oportunidade de desenvolver habilidades e fortalecer a integração entre equipes. sources.text: Nintendo has announced its Black Friday 2026 deals, which include $50 in savings on a “ Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle” and select games at $20-off the suggested retail price. Starting November 22 through December 5, rev up for Black Friday with the “Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle” featuring a Nintendo Switch 2 system, a full download of the Mario Kart World game and a three-month (90-day) Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership for the suggested retail price of $499.99, a savings of $50. Plus, from November 22 through November 29, select games for Nintendo Switch 2 like Donkey Kong Bananza and Nintendo Switch games such as Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 will be $20-off the suggested retail price. All offers available while supplies last. In addition to select retailers, these promotions will be available at the Nintendo New York and Nintendo San Francisco stores. The “Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle” promotion will also be available on the Nintendo Store website. The Nintendo New York and Nintendo San Francisco stores will feature festive window displays and seasonal decor and are a one-stop destination for holiday shopping for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch, plus games, gifts, exclusive items, and more. Share the joy of Nintendo this holiday with exclusive products, collectibles and apparel inspired by your favorite characters and games including Mario , The Legend of Zelda , Animal Crossing , Pikmin , and Splatoon . Holiday gift guides, festive shopping bags, and, for a limited time, a gift with purchase (requires minimum spend) will be available while supplies last. Holiday shoppers looking to get an early jump on enjoying some games can also check out a sale on Nintendo eShop and the Nintendo Store beginning November 19 through December 2.

sources.title: Nintendo Reveals Its Black Friday Sale Plans, With Its Own Games Getting Rare $20 Discounts
sources.text: Black Friday 2026 Nintendo Nintendo Switch 2 Nintendo discounts its in-house games about as often as it warmly encourages downloading ROMs, so it’s something of a big deal to see the announcement that come November 22, games like Donkey Kong Bananza ,Â Metroid Prime 4 , andÂ Kirby Air Riders will all be discounted by $20. The Thanksgiving season will also see the return of theÂ Mario Kart World Switch 2 bundle on November 22, priced at $500, which is the current price of a Switch 2 on its own. You may well remember that when the Switch 2 launched in June 2025, the version bundled with a download code forÂ Mario Kart World was then priced at $500. But in the 18 months since, the price of the Switch 2 has jumped up $50 thanks to the AI-driven component crisis and Trump’s inane tariffs. Thus, returning to the baseline represents something of a bargain in our upside-down times. That bundled deal, which also comes with three months of Nintendo Switch Online, will run from November 22 to December 5, and obviously depends on available stock. For a slightly shorter window, a handful of Nintendo’s own games will also get the Black Friday treatment via retailers like Amazon, Best Buy, GameStop and Walmart, as well as Nintendo’s own U.S. stores. From November 22 to 29, Switch 2 titles Donkey Kong Bananza ,Â Metroid Prime 4: Beyond , Kirby Air Riders , andÂ Super Mario Party Jamboree will all be $20 less, meaning the very splendid Donkey Kong game will be just $50 instead of $70. Meanwhile the Switch versions ofÂ Super Mario Party Jamboree andÂ Metroid Prime 4Â will also receive twenty-buck reductions. Running over yet another set of dates (Nintendo never wants anything to be straightforward), the eShop will be having its own Black Friday sale, this time from November 19 to December 2. So far there are no details about which games will be seeing price drops, but hopefully it’ll see the same titles getting similar discounts. But this is Nintendo, so who knows? Clearly the eShop’s sale will also encompass every other publisher’s games at lower prices too. (Presumably at this point Ubisoft will be paying us to get a copy of Mario vs. Rabbids .) Seeing Nintendo’s own games getting price cuts is not common, especially ones as recent asÂ DK Bananza andÂ Metroid Prime 4 , so if you were waiting on either, this’ll be the time to pounce. sources.title: Nintendo announces its 2026 Black Friday offers, with free games and $20 discounts
sources.text: Nintendo has unveiled its 2026 Black Friday plans Nintendo has officially unveiled its 2026 Black Friday offers today, with discounts across games and consoles landing on November 22. The headline here is that Mario Kart bundle, once again returning to the shelves back in September and now taking a $50 discount when Black Friday Nintendo Switch deals come into full effect at the end of the month. The package comprises the handheld itself ($499.99 MSRP), a copy of Mario Kart World ($79.99 MSRP), and three months of Nintendo Switch Online Individual ($7.99 MSRP), all for $499.99 total. That's not just a $50 discount on the existing bundle price ($549.99 today), but essentially scoring you one of the system's most expensive games for free, plus that NSO membership. Select games have also been highlighted, set to receive $20 discounts when Black Friday offers begin. Right now, we only know that Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Metroid Prime 4 Beyond, Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2, and Super Mario Party Jamboree are taking part in physical discounts across stores like Amazon , Best Buy , GameStop , Target , and Walmart . Digitally, Nintendo has also announced it will be running separate offers via the eShop beginning November 19. We've been tracking early Black Friday offers for a good few weeks now, these are the best discounts available right now. Nintendo Switch 2 | $469 (was $499) at Woot GameSir Super Nova | $29.99 (was $49.99) at Best Buy Metroid Ravenous | $59.88 (was $69.99) at Amazon What's missing here? It would have been a little naive to assume anything Zelda-shaped would be included in this year's Black Friday offers. After all, Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock is still scarce, and Ocarina of Time has set records in just four days on the market . It is a little disheartening to see the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller left out of proceedings, though. The $89 official gamepad leads the charge of the best Nintendo Switch 2 controllers on the market, but hasn't seen a single price cut since launch. It's a premium accessory, but I'm sure we weren't alone in hoping for a saving this holiday season. Nintendo's digital discounts will run through December 2, the reduced price on that Mario Kart World bundle runs through December 5, and those physical game deals will only be available November 22 - November 29. sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Doom Developer id Software Confirms Work on New Game, Will Be Directed by Hugo Martin
sources.text: At Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at its Fan Fest event in Seattle, id Software confirmed that it is working on a new game, wrapping up last year's Doom: The Dark Ages with the release of the upcoming Slaughter Mode on November 16. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma made the announcement on her X account, posting , "Few studios have shaped the first-person shooter genre as much as id Software. Slaughter Mode comes to DOOM: The Dark Ages | Revelations on November 16, and the team is already working on its next game." id itself also posted , saying, "We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on." Whether that next project is more Doom, or perhaps id returning to its other big franchise, Quake, remains to be seen. Or it might be neither of those and could be something new entirely. Although it's worth noting that id Software is under Xbox's Bethesda arm, and Bethesda boss Jill Braff recently told its development teams that "we are shifting from a planning model primarily centered on what's next for each independent studio to one that focuses on our strongest franchises and determining the content roadmap that best serves our players and Bethesda as a whole." So perhaps Quake or a fourth Doom game are the more likely options? That remains to be seen, but what the last decade has proven is that Martin and the id Software team are very good at what they do. Doom (2016) successfully rebooted a dormant franchise, while Doom Eternal stood on its shoulders , and then Doom: The Dark Ages brought the focus back to the ground . All three were excellent. Doom: The Dark Ages' Slaughter Mode, meanwhile, is an endless single-player mode that will be added as a free update for those who've purchased Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations DLC, which we reviewed and loved . Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Id Software Says It’s Working On Its Next Game, Directed By Doom’s Hugo Martin
sources.text: Doom and Wolfenstein studio id Software has begun work on a new project, according to the studio’s official social account , and it’s being directed by Hugo Martin, who previously directed both Doom: The Dark Ages and Doom: Eternal. We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on. — id Software (@idSoftware) November 12, 2026 This news comes over a year after the release of Doom: The Dark Ages . An expansion for The Dark Ages , “Revelations,” was out this past July, and a new “Slaughter Mode” is being implemented on Monday. Martin’s involvement makes it likely that this is yet another Doom game even though that was not explicitly stated, which would be in keeping with Xbox head Asha Sharma’s ambitions to focus on the company’s biggest franchises. Id Software is also the developer of Rage , and Quake , and numerous WolfensteinÂ games (though not the most recent entries in the series). This reassurance as to id Software’s current activities comes on the heels of a mass restructuring at Xbox in July that saw massive swaths of the company cut: over 90 individuals across multiple offices, including a large amount of its id Tech team (claims have suggested only one person was left working on id Tech, but Microsoft has said that is false and that “dozens” of people are working on it). Sources speaking to Kotaku following these layoffs said that the studio didn’t have any new games greenlit at the time, and that concepts kept shifting, suggesting that whatever this new project is, it’s very, very early in development. In the wake of those layoffs, Martin attempted to reassure the public that id Software was in a good spot, noting that the team was now the same size as it was when they made Doom (2016). “Look, the fact that we made a game that people like and is critical and commercially successfulâlike I said, itâs doing very well related to the forecast and stuffâthatâs good for everyone, for the people at the studio, for the people who, unfortunately, we had to say goodbye to, I think that helps everyone and we really appreciate your support,â he said in a livestream. âBut what matters the most is that the the games are good and Iâm so happy that people, I donât knowâ¦ Itâs just a good thing for everybody, itâs going to help.” Just last month, studio co-director Marty Stratton said that id Software was “incredibly viable.” Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. sources.title: Id Software confirms it’s working on a new game after layoffs
sources.text: Asha Sharma says id Software is “already working on its next game”, despite recent layoffs Id Software is working on its next game, Xbox has confirmed. This was revealed as part of the ongoing Xbox FanFest. CEO Asha Sharma confirmed the news on social media, saying that the team at id Software is “already working on its next game” after Doom: The Dark Ages and its recent expansion. However, this also comes shortly after id Software was severely impacted by layoffs across Xbox . 136 workers lost their jobs in total, and it was claimed that id Software had been “ relegated to support studio size “. Xbox seems eager to dispel this claim, announcing a new game from the team before there’s anything to actually show for it. We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on. “We’re incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin ” reads a post made by id Software in response to this announcement. “It’ll be some time before we’re ready to share more but we can’t wait for you to see what we’re working on.” This indicates that the game is in the very early stages of development, as id Software is already trying to ensure that no one expects a trailer anytime soon. That isn’t surprising given how much smaller the team is now, and the fact that it just shipped Doom: The Dark Age’s DLC, Revelations. Hugo Martin has been with id Software since 2013. He was the creative director for Doom (2016) and Doom: Eternal, and the game director for Doom: The Dark Ages. Incidentally, former id Software devs made their own announcement today: the founding of a new studio . Hidden Horses is crowdfunding for its first game, a single-player FPS called Danger Pay. The studio is made up of more than 20 former id Software developers who were caught up in the Xbox layoffs earlier this year.

sources.title: Take-Two CEO Says Discs Will Become Gaming’s Vinyl: ‘It’s Going To Be A Very Small Part Of The Business’
sources.text: Discs GTA 6 Physical Games PlayStation Rockstar Games Vinyl Grand Theft Auto 6 is the first major console game to release without a physical version. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick doesn’t think it’ll be the last. Physical games will hang around, but not in any mass-market sort of way. He says they’ll become closer to the equivalent of vinyl records in music. âIt may not be the end, but listen, weâve been talking, you and I, for a long time,â he told The Game Business ‘ Christopher Dring in a new interview. âI predicted that digital distribution would be well over 90 percent of the business more than 10 years ago. I donât always get it right, but this one I got right. Will there always be some physical business? Yes, in the same way that thereâs still a vinyl business in recorded music. But itâs going to be a very small part of the business.â Physical music accounted for just over 10 percent of total music revenue in the first half of 2026, according to estimates by theÂ Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) . That comes out to $581 million, roughly 80 percent of which was earned through sales of vinyl. According to Circana , physical game sales in the U.S. last year hit a 30-year low of $1.5 billion. That was about 2.5 percent of the $60.7 billion consumers spent on âvideo game hardware, content, and accessoriesâ in 2025. Physical game sales are already a smaller chunk of overall game spending than vinyl is for music, and that’s before PlayStation game discs go away entirely in 2028. Game discs becoming vinyl would actually be a rosier outlook than where things currently seem to be trending. We still don’t know how Microsoft will approach physical media with the launch of its Project Helix family of next-gen consoles, and Nintendo has confirmed it has no plans to abandon physical games during the Switch 2 era, even if it’s already taken a half-step in that direction with game key cards. Will GTA 6 ever get a disc version? Vinyl has been a way for music lovers to immortalize their favorite albums. Surely the biggest game launch ever deserves something similar? Zelnick previously shot down rumors that GTA 6 wasn’t coming to disc. He’s now demurred on whether it could get a physical release in the future. That sort of âinformation always comes from our labels,” he told Variety this week, leaving the ball in Rockstar’s court to decide. GTA 6 is getting a vinyl release for its soundtrack , however. Seem a bit hypocritical? It’s probably less surprising when, as revealed in Take-Two’s latest financials, only 2 percent of its current revenue comes from game discs . sources.name: Insider Gaming
sources.title: Take-Two CEO Says Physical Games Still Have a Future
sources.text: Strauss Zelnick compares physical games to vinyl, saying a small market will remain even as digital makes up 98% of Take-Two ’s business. We are just a week away from the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and while it is a highly anticipated game that is breaking pre-order records, it’s also controversial because it does not have a physical disc release. Despite this, Strauss Zelnick still believes physical media has a place in gaming, and he made his case in a recent interview. Speaking with Christopher Dring of The Game Business , Zelnick compared physical games to the vinyl industry, noting that a group of collectors will always want to own physical versions of the games they play. Still, he stresses that physical media will be a very small part of the video game industry moving forward. “It may not be the end, but listen, we’ve been talking, you and I, for a long time,” he said. “I predicted that digital distribution would be well over 90% of the business more than 10 years ago. I don’t always get it right, but this one I got right. Will there always be some physical business? Yes, in the same way that there’s still a vinyl business in recorded music. But it’s going to be a very small part of the business.” Grand Theft Auto 6 will release on November 19. It will be available on PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series consoles. For those who still have last-gen technology on the XBOX side, Microsoft’s gaming wing recently announced that cloud play is an option for them to experience GTA 6. What do you think? Will physical media always have a place in gaming? Share your thoughts about this story and all others in our official Discord server. For more coverage on Insider Gaming, check out the record-breaking pre-order sales information for Grand Theft Auto 6. Don’t forget to sign up for our weekly newsletter , too. I'm Robert DeFelice.
